beats.title: It opens on your table.
beats.line: A painted pop-up book appears on your real table, and the room dims around it.

beats.title: Reach in.
beats.line: Pip’s lantern blows out. Pick it up, hand it back, and the light comes home.

beats.title: The lighthouse lights your room.
beats.line: When the lamp is lit again, its beam sweeps across your real walls.

storyteller.title: Or make up a new story, out loud.
storyteller.line: Tell Pip, Wick and Moth what tonight's story is about, or hand them something lost. They make it up with you in their own voices, on your table and around your room, and it ends on a page you keep.

Hmph. The old cellar, I’d wager. Nobody’s been down there in years.

about.book: Tales from the Table’s Edge is set in the Lost and Found, where everything lost in a house drifts home to a lighthouse at the edge of the table. Pip is a young fox, afraid of the dark, who quietly wants to be the next keeper. Wick is the grumpy old keeper, secretly losing his sight. Moth flies at anything bright, and brings odd finds.
about.storyteller: Tell Pip, Wick and Moth what tonight's story is about, or hand them something lost, and they make it up with you, out loud. They answer in their own voices, paint the things you ask for, and bring the weather, the stars or the sea into your room. Each story ends on a page in your book, and they remember it next time. Their voices are AI-generated, not people. It needs an account and the internet.
